title: The Architect’s Struggle: Genesis of MetaGit (0 to 1)
description: The definitive chronological account of the sovereign orchestration substrate, sharding the journey from chaotic 'Air' to hardened 'Wood'.

content.executive_summary: MetaGit was forged through a multi-month period of manual architectural strikes, mathematical discovery, and 'Field Hacking'. It represents the movement from ephemeral chat to version-controlled memory across a global network of sovereign sites.
content.physics_of_order: Before MetaGit, state was ephemeral. The Wright Brothers' lesson on control surfaces was applied to AI orchestration: flight requires a hardened State Layer. Unstructured searching (`grep`) is a symptom of the deeper drag, but the MetaGit addresses a broader spectrum of systemic risks identified through forensic analysis of the `dynamic/stream/` and `trash/.chat/` archeology. These include the 'Clio Fracture' (fatal execution loops), the 'Keraunos Freeze' (terminal JavaScript heap exhaustion during high-velocity strikes), and the recurring 'JSON Ingestion/Stringification Stalls' where high-entropy state sharding kills the V8 isolate. Forensic investigation of the `trash/.chat/unclean/` zones reveals a high mortality rate driven by 'Low-Level Binary Fractures' (recurring crashes in `_start` and `libc`) and 'Perceptual Hallucinations' where agents misinterpret terminal noise as user intent. Order had to be engineered before flight could be sustained against this relentless metabolic friction.
